290–630 m² of hall per MW, as five built Canadian halls report (operator claims, mostly 5–10 kW per rack). LBNL's models span 186–2,325.

Small buildings can hold more than this range. With little room for anything else, most of the floor becomes hall: eStruxture VAN-1 puts about 75% of its 929 m² into hall and holds 2.4 MW (operator claim). more

Show the math
Lot area: 17 m² (City parcel data).
Zone floor-space ratio 2 (as if rezoned): 17 × 2 = 34 m².
Storeys under the 18 m height limit: first floor 6.0 m, then data-hall floors of 6.0 or 5.5 m. (18 − 6.0) ÷ 6.0 = 2.00, whole floors 2, plus the first floor = 3; with 5.5 m floors, 2.18 → 2 + 1 = 3.
Footprint from the site setup: the most the zone allows, less setbacks: 12 m² (drawn in 3D).
Most floor area those storeys can hold: 12 m² × 3 = 36 m². The smaller of this and step 2: 34 m².
Data hall: 34 × 0.48 = 16 m², up to 34 × 0.72 = 24 m².
Servers: the smallest hall laid out loosely, 16 ÷ 630 m² per MW = 0.03 MW; the largest hall laid out densely, 24 ÷ 290 = 0.08 MW.
Check: 34 ÷ 1,109 = 0.03 MW; 34 ÷ 505 = 0.07 MW.
Hall share 0.48–0.72: Burlington plan set. 290–630 m² of hall per MW: five built Canadian halls (operator claims). 505–1,109 m² of building per MW: benchmark buildings in the precedent catalogue.

Show the math
Average power at the meter: 0.1 MW × PUE 1.4 = 0.14 MW; × 1.55 = 0.16 MW.
Plant space, dry coolers: (UPS 2–2.4 + batteries 2.2 + dry coolers 24.5) = 28.7–29.1 m² per MW; × 0.1 = 3–3 m².
With heat recovery, add heat pumps 3.4 + CDUs 0.6 = 32.7–33.1 m² per MW; × 0.1 = 3–3 m².
Standby fuel: 0.14–0.16 MW × 1,000 (kW) × 12 h × 0.263 L per kWh = 442–489 L.
PUE: LBNL 2023, Uptime 2025. Plant areas: manufacturer claims, equipment only. Fuel rate: manufacturer claim at full load.

What the heat is worth here
less than nothing: the heat pump costs more to run than the gas it replaces

At Alberta prices (gas $2.50/GJ, power $49.74/MWh) the heat pump's electricity costs more than the gas the heat would replace ($-7.6 to $-2.0 per MWh of heat), so no route pays back at any distance. Each card says what would have to change.

Show the math
Cooling units: power at the meter 0.16 MW, about one unit per MW → 1 unit (an assumption).
Together: Lw per unit 91 (low-noise) to 101 dBA (standard) + 10 × log₁₀(1) = 91.0–101 dBA.
Distance where the night limit is reached: r = 10^((Lw − 8 − 50) ÷ 20) = 45–141 m (free field over hard ground, no walls or barriers).
Jobs: 0.1 MW × 290–630 m² hall per MW ÷ hall share 0.72–0.48 ÷ 464.5 m² per job = 1.00–0.28.
Sound: Lp = Lw − 20 log r − 8 (hemispherical spreading); unit ratings from manufacturer data (Trane, Eurovent). Limits: Noise Control By-law 6555 / Bylaw 14600. Jobs: Virginia JLARC 2024, transferred.

WHO IS NEAR, AND WHAT THEY WOULD NOTICE

WHAT IS SEEN FROM HOMES AND THE STREET

Working out sight lines…

Only the cooling plant and what is on the roof and the facade are tested; backup power, fuel, batteries and electrical equipment are never tested or drawn. Homes: neighbours in quiet (residential) zones within 350 m, from the corner nearest the site at a top-floor window. Street: points every 15 m on the street centrelines within 200 m at 1.6 m eye height (Vancouver; lanes not included); in Edmonton, points 4 m outside the lot.

Sound is a screening estimate: manufacturer-rated levels, no barriers, ground or buildings.
